contributions.title: Prove the exact block-three hook spectrum and error gap (no new κ)
contributions.claim_excerpt:
## Summary

Scoped proof with an exact finite spectral certificate. The block-three hook leakage has squared singular values `0:56, 1/8:48, 5/8:112, 1:64`. In the stated linear, columnwise model, joint operator error strictly below `1/sqrt(8)` requires at least `ceil(14W/5)` paid calls. Five targets with thirteen calls have error at least `1/sqrt(8)`.

```text
exact hook call cap 80
+ exact leakage spectrum
= explicit paid-call versus operator-error obstruction
```

The new result is the spectrum and its quantitative error consequence. Jacob Alan Sussman's #4628 supplies the hook and call-cap theorem as cited premises. Eumemic, Swapnil Jain and lee-phys retain their predecessor credit. No predecessor computation is replayed, and no new kappa or selected-frontier change is claimed. Produced by Nick Petalas. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

## Evidence

Previously the cited hook argument excluded exact completion below `14W/5`. The new certificate proves a positive error gap using an integer 280-square Gram matrix:

```text
A(A-I)(A-5I)(A-8I) = 0
tr(A^0),tr(A^1),tr(A^2),tr(A^3) = 280,1120,6944,46816
```

All 78,400 leakage entries are regenerated from Walsh minors. ~~~text
coker_D G_f = (D/(3))^a direct-sum (D/(15))^b
safe inverse-input fraction = 9^(-a-b) * 25^(-b)
least odd denominator for unrestricted exact inputs = 15
~~~

contributions.head: 0cb79c588655cc85653ca4123c74fe3cc42c6ec9
contributions.title: Prove the nonlinear boundary of the abelian no-phase reduction (no new κ)
contributions.claim_excerpt:
## Summary

A nonlinear address permutation cannot be absorbed into the abelian no-phase reduction used in Jacob Alan Sussman's #4628. This scoped proof identifies the exact boundary for every binary address dimension:

```text
P A P^-1 = A  <=>  p(x) = Mx+t, M invertible
p nonlinear  =>  <A, P A P^-1> is nonabelian
```

The second conclusion rules out every larger abelian group containing the original calls and normalized by that permutation. An explicit three-bit Toffoli commutator witnesses the obstruction. This applies the elementary translation-normalizer argument to the cited reduction; it does not claim a new abstract normalizer technique, actual nonlinear-program tariff, supplier or κ.

The contribution was produced by Nick Petalas. Sussman's semidirect-product reduction and the retained eumemic #288 / Swapnil Jain P1/P2 lineage receive credit. Predecessor results are cited, not replayed. Exact source paths, commits and hashes are in `SOURCES.json`.

## Evidence

- Before: #4628 section 5 absorbs linear address maps into register copies, with no classification here of nonlinear extensions.
- After: a self-contained dimension-uniform proof, including impossibility of an abelian enlargement. A complete census checks all 40,320 three-bit permutations: exactly 1,344 normalizers and a checked noncommutation witness for each of the other 38,976. One- and two-bit censuses give 2/2 and 24/24.
- Literal eight-by-eight Gaussian-integer checks verify every three-bit call-root square and the Toffoli call-root noncommutation. Four false mathematical claims are rejected in both n

contributions.claim_excerpt:
## Summary

Prove a scoped classification of exact carried-frame rounding. For every integer d >= 1, refinement m >= 2 and group G <= GL_d(Z),

```text
uniformly bounded G-equivariant q : (1/m)Z^d -> Z^d
                         exists iff G is finite
```

The d seed errors form an integer matrix congruent to -I modulo m; its invertibility bounds every frame matrix. For finite G, a construction on all of R^d rounds into the lattice fixed by each canonical orbit point's stabilizer. It fixes integer inputs and needs no continuity or coordinatewise rule.

This extends Sricharan Vagvala's merged #1631 shear obstruction and addresses the compatibility concern in woklerx's merged #1892. Sagar Thakrar #1537, Ross Richardson #1287 and the retained frame/dirty-echo lineage keep their credit. The new contribution is produced by Nick Petalas. No predecessor verifier is imported or replayed.

## Evidence

Before: one shear obstruction and separate orbit-window optima. After: a dimension-uniform equivalence and a compatible positive construction.
